questions.q: You are the first to arrive at the scene of a road accident on a rural highway. One vehicle is in a ditch. What do you do first?
options: Stop right in your lane by the ditch and immediately run across the road to the vehicle
Stop safely, switch on the hazard warning lights, put out the warning triangle and assess the danger
First film the accident scene on video to give the recording to the police later
Drive past so as not to get in the way, and phone a friend to ask what to do
questions.explain: Make yourself and the accident scene safe first, otherwise there will be more casualties: stop in a safe place, switch on the hazard warning lights and assess the danger (Highway Code UK, para. 283). Outside a built-up area, put out the warning triangle not closer than 30 m from the vehicle ⟦32⟧.

questions.q: What number can you call in Kazakhstan for help for someone injured in a road accident?
questions.explain: Call an ambulance on 103, and other emergency services on 112 (First Aid Rules of the Republic of Kazakhstan, para. 16). Under the list of emergency services, 104 and 109 are emergency utility and municipal services, 111 is the contact centre for family, women and children's issues, and 1414 is the contact centre for government services.
questions.ref: First Aid Rules of the Republic of Kazakhstan, para. 16; list of emergency services (Resolution of the Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan)

questions.q: You call 112 from the scene of a road accident on a highway. What is the best way to start the conversation with the dispatcher?
options: With the exact location: highway, kilometre marker, direction and landmarks
With the make, colour and number plates of all the damaged vehicles
With who you think is to blame for the accident
With your own surname, first name, age and place of work or study
questions.explain: Without the exact location, the crew will not find the accident, and if the call is cut off, the location will already be known. Then say what happened, how many casualties there are and what condition they are in, and do not hang up first (First Aid Rules of the Republic of Kazakhstan, para. 16; Highway Code UK, para. 283).

questions.q: A driver in a vehicle does not answer questions and does not respond to touch. He is taking occasional gasping breaths. What does this mean and what should you do?
options: Since he is breathing, it is not cardiac arrest: watch him and wait for the ambulance
This is fainting: give him smelling salts to sniff, tap his cheeks and wait for the ambulance
This is shock: cover him and give him small sips of warm water
This is cardiac arrest: call 112 or 103 and start compressions
questions.explain: The person is not responding and is not breathing normally, which means he is in cardiac arrest. Infrequent gasping (“agonal”) breaths are not normal breathing ⟦33⟧. For compressions, lay him on his back on a firm surface.

questions.q: How should you correctly give chest compressions to an adult?
options: Depth 2-3 cm, about 60 compressions a minute
Depth 5-6 cm, 100-120 compressions a minute
Depth 8-10 cm, as fast as possible
Depth 5-6 cm, 60-80 compressions a minute
questions.explain: Press on the centre of the chest to a depth of 5-6 cm at a rate of 100-120 per minute, and let the chest fully recoil after each compression.

questions.q: You have started resuscitation, but you do not know how to give rescue breaths and are not willing to give them. What should you do?
options: Stop resuscitation: without breaths it is useless, better to wait for the ambulance
Alternate 5 compressions with a 10-second pause to let blood flow back
Give continuous chest compressions only, until help arrives
Stop the compressions and just tap his cheeks until he wakes up
questions.explain: If you are not trained to give breaths or are not willing to give them, perform continuous compressions without interruptions ⟦34⟧. A trained rescuer alternates 30 compressions with 2 breaths.

questions.q: A driver in a car park feels unwell and loses consciousness. There are no signs of injury, and he is breathing normally. What should you do after calling an ambulance?
options: Turn him into the recovery position and monitor his breathing
Start chest compressions immediately and do not stop until the ambulance arrives
Sit him up against the car and give him sweet water to drink
Leave him lying on his back facing up and step away so as not to disturb him
questions.explain: A person with reduced consciousness due to illness, with no signs of injury, who is breathing normally, is placed in the recovery position ⟦35⟧. If breathing becomes abnormal, start resuscitation.

questions.q: After a rear-end collision, a passenger is conscious and complains of severe neck pain. The vehicle is not on fire, and the road is closed off. What should you do?
options: Pull him out of the vehicle and lay him on the ground with a jacket under his head
Ask him to turn his head to check whether his neck can move
Sit him up straighter and tilt his head back onto the headrest
Ask him not to move, to keep his head still, and wait for the medics
questions.explain: If a neck injury is suspected, movement of the neck is kept to a minimum: a conscious person holds their own head in a comfortable, stable position ⟦36⟧. Without a threat of fire or a further collision, they are not pulled out of the vehicle (Highway Code UK, para. 283).

questions.q: A casualty has severe bleeding from a wound on the shin. You press firmly on the wound through cloth, but blood keeps gushing out. You have a tourniquet. How should you apply it?
options: Right on the knee, tighten it as hard as possible, no need to record the time
5-7 cm above the wound, not over a joint, tighten it until the bleeding stops, and record the time
5-7 cm below the wound, closer to the foot, and tighten it until the leg turns pale
Above the wound, but loosely, so the leg does not turn blue, and loosen it every 15 minutes
questions.explain: A tourniquet is applied for life-threatening bleeding from a limb, when pressure does not help: 5-7 cm above the wound, not over a joint, and it is tightened until the bleeding stops. The time is recorded, and the tourniquet is not loosened: only medics remove it ⟦37⟧.

questions.q: While putting out a small fire, a driver burns his hand. What is the right thing to do?
options: Apply ice or snow for about 20 minutes, then bandage the whole hand tightly
Immediately rub on oil or a greasy cream and cover it with cotton wool
Cool it with cool running water for at least 20 minutes, and remove any rings
Burst the blisters, rinse with alcohol and bandage the hand tightly
questions.explain: A burn is cooled immediately with cool running water: at least 20 minutes under ANZCOR and Highway Code UK (the First Aid Standard of the Republic of Kazakhstan says at least 15 minutes). Ice, oils and creams are not allowed, and blisters are not burst. Rings are removed before swelling starts, and the burn is then loosely covered with a clean material.

questions.q: A casualty's forearm is unnaturally bent, and he is conscious. An ambulance is already on its way. What do you do?
options: Immobilise the arm in the position you found it in, without trying to straighten it
Sharply straighten the arm so the bone goes back into place, and tie it to a board
Ask him to move his fingers and his whole arm to assess the fracture
Tightly tie a tourniquet around the forearm above the injury to prevent swelling
questions.explain: A broken limb is not straightened or set; it is immobilised in the position found, supporting the areas above and below the injury (First Aid Standard of the Republic of Kazakhstan, para. 8; MedlinePlus). A tourniquet is needed only for life-threatening bleeding.

questions.q: After a road accident, a casualty is pale, his skin is cold and clammy, his pulse is fast, he is restless and asks for water. What is correct?
options: Give him a cup of hot sweet tea to drink and cover him up so that he warms up
Sit him up and ask him to walk around a little so that he comes back to himself
Give him a painkiller tablet and some water to relieve his pain and his thirst
Lay him down, cover him and give him nothing to eat or drink until the medics arrive
questions.explain: These are signs of shock. The person is laid down and covered to keep them warm. Nothing is given by mouth: no food, no drink and no tablets (MedlinePlus; Highway Code UK, Annex 7).

questions.q: You decide to help at the scene of a road accident on a rural road. Where is the best place to stop your vehicle?
options: Right up against the damaged vehicles, on the carriageway itself, with hazard lights on
Across the road in front of the accident, to block traffic for everyone
In a safe place, not blocking the path of the ambulance, and switch on the hazard warning lights
On the opposite shoulder facing the accident, so it is convenient to film it
questions.explain: The main danger after an accident is a further collision. Stop in a relatively safe place so that you do not obstruct the ambulance or the rescue services, switch on the hazard warning lights and put out the warning triangle (Highway Code UK, para. 283; paras. 44 and 45 of the Rules).

questions.q: What are considered the main dangers immediately after a road accident?
options: Broken glass on the road
Further collisions and fire
Loud engine noise
Curious bystanders
questions.explain: According to Highway Code UK, the main dangers after an accident are further collisions and fire. So first warn other drivers, ask them to switch off the engines of the damaged vehicles, and not to smoke nearby.

questions.q: Fuel is leaking from under a damaged vehicle. What should you do first?
options: First cover the puddle with sand, and leave people in the vehicles until the rescuers arrive
Start the damaged vehicle and drive it away from the fuel puddle
Wash the fuel off the road with water from bottles so that it does not catch fire
Switch off the ignition, keep away fire and smoking, and move people away
questions.explain: Spilled fuel can ignite from a spark or a cigarette. Switch off the engine, do not let anyone smoke, and move uninjured people well away from the vehicles and the carriageway (Highway Code UK, para. 283).

questions.q: You stop at the scene of a road accident in a town. How far from your vehicle should you put out the warning triangle?
options: Not closer than 15 m
Not closer than 5 m
Right at the rear bumper
Not closer than 100 m
questions.explain: The triangle is placed so that other drivers have time to notice the danger: not closer than 15 m from the vehicle in a built-up area, and not closer than 30 m outside a built-up area.

questions.q: The passengers of the second vehicle are unhurt and are standing on the carriageway next to the wrecked vehicles. What should you advise them to do?
options: Stay by the vehicles so the police can see the people involved in the accident straight away
Get back into the wrecked vehicle and fasten their seat belts until the police arrive
Pick up the debris from the road so that other vehicles do not get punctured tyres
Move off the carriageway to a safe place well away from the traffic
questions.explain: Uninjured people are moved away from the vehicles to a safe place, well away from the carriageway: passing vehicles could hit them (Highway Code UK, para. 283). Those involved do not move items relating to the accident ⟦38⟧.

questions.q: You need to press on the bleeding wound of a stranger. What should you do before that, if possible?
options: Put on gloves from the first aid kit, or at least protect your hand with a plastic bag
First examine the wound and pull out all the pieces of glass from it
Nothing: gloves only get in the way, and you cannot afford to lose a single second
First find the casualty's documents so you can give the details to the dispatcher
questions.explain: Gloves protect both you and the casualty from infection, and they are included in the first aid kit. If you do not have gloves, a plastic bag will do, and a conscious person can press on the wound themselves (American Red Cross). Objects stuck in a wound are not removed.
questions.ref: American Red Cross; contents of the first aid kit (Order of the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 118/2020)

questions.q: A vehicle with a casualty inside starts to catch fire. The casualty is conscious and complains of neck pain. What should you do?
options: Do not touch him because of the neck injury, and wait for the fire service by the vehicle
First fit him with a cervical collar, then call the rescue service
Get him out immediately, moving his head and neck as little as possible
Pour water from a bottle over the vehicle and leave him inside until help arrives
questions.explain: Casualties are not pulled out of vehicles unless necessary, but fire is an immediate threat to life, and that matters more than the risk to the spine (Highway Code UK, para. 283). Get them out with two people if possible, keeping the head and neck in line with the torso.

questions.q: There is zero balance on the phone. Can you still call the emergency services?
options: No: you must top up the balance by at least a small amount first
Yes: connecting to the emergency services is free of charge
Only through a messaging app, if the phone has an internet connection
Only if you have a plan with the operator that covers this road
questions.explain: Connecting to the emergency services (101, 102, 103, 104, 112) is free for subscribers: this is set out in the list of emergency services approved by the Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan. Call an ambulance on 103, and other services on 112.
questions.ref: List of emergency services with free connection (Resolution of the Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan); First Aid Rules of the Republic of Kazakhstan, para. 16

questions.q: The 112 dispatcher already knows where the road accident happened. What else is important to report?
options: The make, colour and year of manufacture of all the vehicles that collided on the road
Who you think is to blame and how fast the vehicles were going
The insurance policy numbers and owner details of all the vehicles
How many casualties there are, whether they are breathing, and whether there is severe bleeding
questions.explain: The dispatcher uses this information to decide how many crews and which services to send. Also say how many vehicles were involved in the collision, whether anyone is trapped in a vehicle, and whether there is fire or leaking fuel (First Aid Rules of the Republic of Kazakhstan, para. 16; Highway Code UK, para. 283).

questions.q: You are calling an ambulance, and an unconscious person is lying next to you. What is the best way to talk to the dispatcher?
options: Briefly describe the situation and hang up straight away so as not to tie up the line
Move well away from the casualty so the dispatcher can hear you better
Switch on the loudspeaker and follow the dispatcher's instructions
Hand the phone to a random passer-by and go and fetch the first aid kit yourself
questions.explain: With the loudspeaker on, your hands stay free: you can check breathing and give compressions while the dispatcher tells you what to do ⟦39⟧. Do not hang up until the dispatcher tells you to.
